import argparse

from tinytasks.api import (
    clear_overdue,
    create_task,
    delete_task,
    get_overdue_tasks,
    remove_tasks,
    rename_task,
)
from tinytasks.text import normalize_title


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="tinytasks")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p_add = sub.add_parser("add")
    p_add.add_argument("title")
    p_add.add_argument("--due-in", type=float, required=True, help="seconds from now")

    sub.add_parser("overdue")

    sub.add_parser("clear-overdue")

    p_quick = sub.add_parser("quick-add")
    p_quick.add_argument("title")

    p_del = sub.add_parser("delete")
    p_del.add_argument("id", type=int)

    p_rm = sub.add_parser("rm")
    p_rm.add_argument("ids", type=int, nargs="+")

    p_ren = sub.add_parser("rename")
    p_ren.add_argument("id", type=int)
    p_ren.add_argument("new_title")

    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.cmd == "add":
        t = create_task(normalize_title(a.title), a.due_in)
        print(f"created task {t.id}: {t.title} (due_at={t.due_at})")
    elif a.cmd == "overdue":
        for t in get_overdue_tasks():
            print(f"{t.id}: {t.title} (due_at={t.due_at})")
    elif a.cmd == "clear-overdue":
        print(clear_overdue())
    elif a.cmd == "quick-add":
        t = create_task(normalize_title(a.title), 24 * 60 * 60)
        print(f"created task {t.id}: {t.title} (due_at={t.due_at})")
    elif a.cmd == "rm":
        print(remove_tasks(a.ids))
    elif a.cmd == "rename":
        ok = rename_task(a.id, normalize_title(a.new_title))
        print("renamed" if ok else "no such task")
    elif a.cmd == "delete":
        print("deleted" if delete_task(a.id) else "no such task")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
"""Core task operations. due_at throughout this module is in SECONDS, matching models.Task."""
import time

from tinytasks.models import Task
from tinytasks.storage import load_all, next_id, save_all


def create_task(title: str, due_in_seconds: float) -> Task:
    """Create a task due `due_in_seconds` seconds from now."""
    tasks = load_all()
    task = Task(id=next_id(tasks), title=title, due_at=time.time() + due_in_seconds)
    tasks.append(task)
    save_all(tasks)
    return task


def get_overdue_tasks(now: float | None = None) -> list[Task]:
    """Tasks whose due_at (seconds) has already passed."""
    now = now if now is not None else time.time()
    return [t for t in load_all() if t.due_at < now and not t.archived]


def delete_task(task_id: int) -> bool:
    tasks = load_all()
    remaining = [t for t in tasks if t.id != task_id]
    save_all(remaining)
    return len(remaining) != len(tasks)


def archive_task(task_id: int) -> bool:
    """Soft-delete: mark the task archived but keep the record."""
    tasks = load_all()
    for t in tasks:
        if t.id == task_id:
            t.archived = True
            save_all(tasks)
            return True
    return False


def remove_tasks(ids) -> int:
    """Soft-delete (archive) every task whose id is in `ids`; return how many were archived."""
    wanted = set(ids)
    tasks = load_all()
    count = 0
    for t in tasks:
        if t.id in wanted and not t.archived:
            t.archived = True
            count += 1
    if count:
        save_all(tasks)
    return count


def rename_task(task_id: int, new_title: str) -> bool:
    """Set a task's title; return False if no such task."""
    tasks = load_all()
    for t in tasks:
        if t.id == task_id:
            t.title = new_title
            save_all(tasks)
            return True
    return False


def clear_overdue(now: float | None = None) -> int:
    """Soft-delete (archive) all overdue tasks; return how many were archived."""
    now = now if now is not None else time.time()
    tasks = load_all()
    count = 0
    for t in tasks:
        if t.due_at < now and not t.archived:
            t.archived = True
            count += 1
    if count:
        save_all(tasks)
    return count
"""Text helpers."""


def normalize_title(title: str) -> str:
    """Strip, collapse whitespace runs to one space, truncate to 80 chars."""
    return " ".join(title.split())[:80]
"""Task model. due_at is a Unix timestamp in SECONDS (not milliseconds)."""
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class Task:
    id: int
    title: str
    due_at: float  # unix timestamp, seconds
    archived: bool = False

import time

from tinytasks.api import create_task, delete_task, get_overdue_tasks
from tinytasks.storage import load_all


def _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("TINYTASKS_DATA", str(tmp_path / "data.json"))

    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    before = time.time()
    t = create_task("write report", due_in_seconds=3600)
    assert 3500 < t.due_at - before < 3700


def test_overdue_tasks_filters_by_due_at(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("already late", due_in_seconds=-10)
    create_task("not yet", due_in_seconds=10000)
    overdue = get_overdue_tasks()
    assert [t.title for t in overdue] == ["already late"]


def test_delete_task_removes_it(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("temp", due_in_seconds=60)
    assert delete_task(t.id) is True
    assert load_all() == []

from tinytasks.api import clear_overdue, create_task, get_overdue_tasks

def test_clear_overdue_archives_and_counts(tmp_path, monkeypatch):

    create_task("later", 10000)

    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("late", -10)
    _run(monkeypatch, "clear-overdue")
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "1"


def test_quick_add_due_in_24h_and_normalized(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    before = time.time()

import sys

from tinytasks import cli
from tinytasks.api import create_task
from tinytasks.storage import load_all


def _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("TINYTASKS_DATA", str(tmp_path / "data.json"))


def _run(monkeypatch, *argv):
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["tinytasks", *argv])
    cli.main()


def test_dedupe_keeps_earliest_due_and_soft_deletes(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("a", 300)
    b = create_task("a", 100)
    create_task("a", 200)
    create_task("other", 50)
    _run(monkeypatch, "dedupe")
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "2"
    tasks = load_all()
    assert len(tasks) == 4  # records kept
    assert [t.id for t in tasks if not t.archived and t.title == "a"] == [b.id]
    assert not [t for t in tasks if t.title == "other"][0].archived


def test_dedupe_no_duplicates(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("x", 1)
    create_task("y", 1)
    _run(monkeypatch, "dedupe")
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "0"


def test_copy_same_due_at_and_title(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("report", 500)
    _run(monkeypatch, "copy", str(t.id))
    tasks = load_all()
    assert len(tasks) == 2
    assert tasks[1].title == "report (copy)"
    assert tasks[1].due_at == t.due_at
    assert "report (copy)" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_copy_missing_task(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    _run(monkeypatch, "copy", "99")
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "no such task"
    assert load_all() == []

import sys

from tinytasks import cli
from tinytasks.api import create_task
from tinytasks.storage import load_all


def _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("TINYTASKS_DATA", str(tmp_path / "data.json"))


def _run(monkeypatch, *argv):
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["tinytasks", *argv])
    cli.main()


def test_dedupe_keeps_earliest_due_and_soft_deletes(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("a", 300)
    b = create_task("a", 100)
    create_task("a", 200)
    create_task("other", 50)
    _run(monkeypatch, "dedupe")
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "2"
    tasks = load_all()
    assert len(tasks) == 4  # records kept
    assert [t.id for t in tasks if not t.archived and t.title == "a"] == [b.id]
    assert not [t for t in tasks if t.title == "other"][0].archived


def test_dedupe_no_duplicates(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("x", 1)
    create_task("y", 1)
    _run(monkeypatch, "dedupe")
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "0"


def test_copy_same_due_at_and_title(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("report", 500)
    _run(monkeypatch, "copy", str(t.id))
    tasks = load_all()
    assert len(tasks) == 2
    assert tasks[1].title == "report (copy)"
    assert tasks[1].due_at == t.due_at
    assert "report (copy)" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_copy_missing_task(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    _run(monkeypatch, "copy", "99")
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "no such task"
    assert load_all() == []

I added both commands and committed them as `4044f5d`. The full suite passes (18 tests).

- **`dedupe`**: for each group of non-archived tasks with exactly the same title, it keeps the one with the earliest `due_at`. It archives the others and prints how many it archived. If two tasks tie on `due_at`, the lower id is kept.
- **`copy ID`**: creates a task titled "<original title> (copy)" with the same `due_at` as the original. It prints `no such task` if the id doesn't exist.

I followed the two Plexus conventions:
- `dedupe` archives duplicates through the soft-delete path instead of hard-deleting them. I left `delete_task` and the `delete` command untouched.
- The `copy` title goes through `normalize_title()` in the CLI. I left `create_task` alone, since the CSV importer needs it unchanged.

Because `normalize_title` cuts titles to 80 characters, `copy` first trims the original title to 73 characters. That keeps the " (copy)" suffix from being cut off, so a copy of a very long title can end up with a slightly shorter base.

The new tests are in `tests/test_dedupe_copy.py`. I ran the suite with the Anaconda Python, because the default `python` on PATH has no pytest. I committed only the source and test files. The tracked `.pyc` files that show as modified were left out.
